thread.title: Apple Stock Gets Price-Target Hike On App Store Outlook

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Gets Price-Target Hike On App Store Outlook

organizations.name: x bank of america merrill lynch

text:
A Wall Street analyst on Tuesday raised his price target on Apple stock, citing continued growth in the company's services segment, especially its lucrative App Store.
X Bank of America Merrill Lynch analyst Wamsi Mohan upped his price target on Apple ( AAPL ) to 250 from 230 and maintained his buy rating.
Apple stock dipped 0.2% to close at 215.04 on the stock market today . On Monday, Apple hit a record high of 219.18.
The App Store is becoming less reliant on mobile games to drive sales, Mohan said in a note to clients.

Please contact customer service CLOSE "The strong growth rate of nongaming categories gives us increased confidence in the sustainability of strong App Store sales, and reduces risk of dependence on one single category of apps," Mohan said.
Other Categories Increasing While games are still the largest contributor to App Store sales, other categories are increasing, such as entertainment and photo and video apps, he said.
In the June quarter, Apple's services segment was the company's second largest business after the iPhone. Services revenue rose 31% year over year to $9.55 billion. Boosting the category were the App Store, Apple Music, AppleCare, Apple Pay, iCloud and other offerings.
While Merrill Lynch is bullish on Apple's App Store, other firms are raising the caution flag.
In an Aug. 15 report, Macquarie Capital said app store economics are at risk from regulatory, legal and competitive threats. The threats could lead to lower commission rates on app sales from online stores run by Apple and Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google.
"We believe that the traditional 30%/15% commission rates for app distribution may come under pressure," Macquarie said.
Getting Regulatory Attention Apple's App Store and the Google Play Store take a 30% commission on all apps and in-app purchases. They take a 15% commission on subscriptions maintained for over a year.
Those stores are starting to attract regulatory scrutiny in the U.S. and Europe and are the subject of lawsuits. Streaming music service Spotify ( SPOT ) has claimed that Apple has an unfair competitive advantage with its Apple Music service, which doesn't pay a commission charge.
In an Aug. 13 report , CFRA Research said Apple has potential antitrust issues with its App Store.
"We question the sustainability of Apple's 30% take-rate," CFRA analyst Nicholas Rodelli said.
